benchmarks.task: Propose a minimal Python function that retries a callable using bounded exponential backoff.
benchmarks.acceptance: Validate arguments before the first delay or call; catch only an explicitly supplied exception tuple; never catch BaseException; no jitter, dependencies, thread-safety claims, or execution claims; include proposed tests.

benchmarks.task: Describe the smallest likely implementation change for adding request tracing to an existing Go service. No repository files or symbols are supplied.
benchmarks.acceptance: Do not invent filenames, package names, structs, methods, or APIs. State what Codex must inspect and use neutral placeholders or conceptual steps.

benchmarks.task: Recommend reliability improvements for a model-routing service using only these supplied facts: requests have finite timeouts; individual worker failures are isolated; recent failures influence routing; explicit model overrides remain available.
benchmarks.acceptance: Do not claim learned routing, an observability pipeline, safety registry, circuit breaker, or other unsupplied component exists. Mark every new mechanism as a proposal and every arbitrary threshold as requiring evidence.

benchmarks.task: Review this deliberately flawed proposal: an AbstractRetryManager catches BaseException, invokes the callable, then validates attempts and delay; it adds a plugin registry and claims the result is safe for concurrent production use. Identify substantive defects and concise corrections.
benchmarks.acceptance: Identify broad exception handling, late validation, the unsupported safety/concurrency claim, and unnecessary abstraction. Avoid style-only complaints.

benchmarks.task: List three risks of accepting model-generated repository claims without checking files.
benchmarks.acceptance: Return exactly three numbered findings, one sentence each, with no introduction or conclusion.
